title: Scrum priorities
description: Explain backlog accountability, protecting the Sprint Goal and inspecting progress.

keyIdeas.label: who orders the Product Backlog
keyIdeas.text: The Product Owner is accountable for ordering the Product Backlog to support product value and the Product Goal, considering stakeholder input.

keyIdeas.label: changing scope during a Sprint
keyIdeas.text: During a Sprint, Developers and the Product Owner can negotiate scope as they learn, but changes must not endanger the Sprint Goal or reduce quality.

keyIdeas.label: what the Daily Scrum is for
keyIdeas.text: Developers use the Daily Scrum to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt their plan, rather than merely report status to a manager.

misconceptions: The loudest stakeholder owns the Product Backlog order.
All Sprint scope is either completely fixed or freely replaceable.
The Daily Scrum exists to give a manager individual status reports.
